title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2611.21969v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding conversational interactions between mothers and children is an important challenge for computational behavioral modeling. Existing methods use traditional statistical approaches and subjective measures of conversational dynamics, without incorporating temporal or probabilistic modeling. We developed an interpretable computational framework that combines sequence analysis, information-theoretic measures, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play. translated_title: 轮到我了！可解释方法揭示母子对话动态中的发展差异
translated_abstract: 理解母亲与儿童之间的对话互动是计算行为建模的一项重要挑战。现有方法采用传统统计方法和对话动态的主观测量，未纳入时间或概率建模。我们开发了一个可解释的计算框架，结合序列分析、信息论测度和贝叶斯层次建模来刻画亲子游戏中的时间性对话动态。我们将该框架应用于94对母亲与两岁儿童的双向互动数据。序列分析显示，与高发展组相比，语言发展水平较低的双向组（以贝利发育量表分数定义）表现出更加异质性的对话组织和更少的“一来一回”式交流，即一种伙伴双方轮流发起交流的互惠式轮流模式。
tldr: 该研究开发了一个结合序列分析、信息论测度和贝叶斯层次建模的可解释计算框架，揭示了语言发展较低的两岁儿童与母亲的对话表现出更异质的组织结构和更少的互惠式轮流交流。
en_tdlr: This study develops an interpretable computational framework combining sequence analysis, information-theoretic measures, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling, revealing that mother-child dyads with lower language development exhibit more heterogeneous conversational organization and fewer reciprocal serve-and-return exchanges.
